predecessors.name: Kingdom of Lagos
predecessors.text: Lagos, ceded by Oba Dosunmu (Docemo) in the Lagos Treaty of Cession after 11 days' resistance

successors.name: Niger Coast Protectorate
successors.text: the Lagos Colony and its protectorate over most of Yorubaland, 'amalgamated as the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria' on 28 February 1906

ledger.x: 1891 (13 August): Ilaro comes under British protection.
1892: Ijebu Ode is captured and the Awujale surrenders 'shortly afterward' (no month on the page).
1892: the Ijebu kingdom passes under the Lagos Colony's protectorate.
1893 (3 February): the Alafin of Oyo accepts British protection.
1906 (28 February): the Yoruba protectorate is merged with Southern Nigeria.
1906 (28 February): Ijebu becomes part of the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria.
1906 (28 February): Oyo becomes part of the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria.
1906 (28 February): Ibadan becomes part of the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria.
1906 (28 February): Lagos is amalgamated with Southern Nigeria.
1906 (28 February): the Lagos Colony ends; Lagos becomes the administrative centre of Southern Nigeria.

wars.name: Ijebu Expedition
wars.outcome: British victory: landing at Epe 12 May 1892, Ijebu Ode captured.

certainty.note: No area and no boundary on the page; the colony proper is a circle round Lagos, the protectorate states are circles round their capitals.
